Defect Title: Public Unauthenticated Read Access to Orders Collection (BOLA / Sensitive Data Exposure)
Description: In firestore.rules (lines 41-46), the orders collection is configured with "allow read: if true;". Any unauthenticated internet user can dump or query every customer order record in the database, exposing customer names, phone numbers, delivery addresses, order contents, payment proof, and event dates.
Expected Result: Firestore should reject unauthenticated queries and allow customers to read only their own orders (request.auth.uid == resource.data.customerUid), while administrators have full read access.
Actual Result: Firestore returns the complete collection of customer orders to any anonymous visitor.
Technical Impact: Complete exposure of Customer Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and purchase history; OWASP Top 10 A01:2021 (Broken Access Control).
Business Impact: Severe regulatory breach, privacy violation, risk of targeted customer scams, and brand reputation destruction.
Remediation Recommendation: Update firestore.rules to restrict order reads: match /orders/{orderId} { allow read: if (request.auth != null && (request.auth.token.admin == true || resource.data.customerUid == request.auth.uid)); allow create: if true; }

Defect Title: Arbitrary Admin Privilege Escalation via Unrestricted admins Collection Write Access
Description: In firestore.rules (lines 6-8), the admins collection specifies "allow read, write: if request.auth != null;". In AuthContext.jsx (lines 93-102), any user with a record in admins/{uid} is treated as an administrator. Any user who signs up or logs in via Google can write their own UID into admins and immediately gain full Administrative portal access.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Sign in as a regular customer with a standard personal Google account.
2. Open DevTools Console.
3. Run: await setDoc(doc(db, "admins", auth.currentUser.uid), { role: "admin", isActive: true });
4. Navigate to /admin.
Expected Result: Only pre-authorized superadministrators should be permitted to create or modify administrator profiles in the database.
Actual Result: Any authenticated user can elevate themselves to full Administrator and modify/delete catalog products, orders, CMS content, and payment settings.
Technical Impact: Total compromise of administrative authorization boundary; arbitrary catalog manipulation and order tampering.
Business Impact: Hostile takeover of bakery operations, falsification of payment settings (diverting bank transfers), and unauthorized database purging.
Remediation Recommendation: Implement Firebase Custom Claims (e.g. token.admin == true) set via Cloud Function / Admin SDK, and lock firestore.rules: match /admins/{adminId} { allow read, write: if request.auth.token.admin == true; }

Defect Title: Silent Order Loss: Checkout Reports Order Success Even If Firestore Database Save Fails
Description: In CheckoutPage.jsx (lines 123-129), the Firestore addDoc(collection(db, "orders"), fullOrderData) call is wrapped in a try/catch that merely logs a console warning and allows execution to proceed to setIsSuccess(true). If database save fails, the user is given an Order Number, but zero order record exists in the database.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Simulate a Firestore write failure (e.g., test with offline network state or security rule rejection).
2. Submit an order on /cart.
3. Observe UI response.
4. Check database for record.
Expected Result: If database persistence fails, checkout must abort, display an explicit error to the customer, and retain cart items for retry.
Actual Result: UI displays "Order Placed Successfully! Order #: GNC-..." and clears the cart, while no order was recorded in the database.
Technical Impact: Inability to audit, track, or fulfill customer orders; transactions vanish without trace.
Business Impact: Customers pay or wait for deliveries that the bakery never received, causing angry customers, lost revenue, and operational chaos.
Remediation Recommendation: Make database persistence a mandatory blocking precondition for order success: if addDoc fails, throw error, alert customer, and do not clear cart.

Defect Title: Missing Essential HTTP Security Headers in Production (Clickjacking, MIME Sniffing, CSP Risks)
Description: Live HTTP probe of https://goodnews-cake-and-catering.vercel.app/ reveals that Vercel is configured with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, but lacks Content-Security-Policy (CSP), X-Frame-Options (DENY), X-Content-Type-Options (nosniff), Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy.
Expected Result: Production headers should include X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin, and Content-Security-Policy.
Actual Result: Headers are completely absent from vercel.json configuration.
Technical Impact: Site is vulnerable to Clickjacking (embedding in malicious iframes), MIME-type confusion attacks, and unconstrained script loading.
Business Impact: Phishing attacks impersonating the bakery, credential theft from embedded iframes, and compliance failure.
Remediation Recommendation: Add comprehensive headers block to vercel.json specifying X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, and strict CSP.

Defect Title: Missing Cloud Storage Security Rules Specification & Client-Side Only MIME Validation
Description: In storageService.js (lines 4-24), file validation is performed solely in browser JavaScript (checking file.type and file.size). The repository contains no storage.rules file defining backend security constraints on the Firebase Storage bucket.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Inspect repository root for storage.rules.
2. Review storageService.js validation logic.
Expected Result: Storage rules should be checked into source control (storage.rules) restricting uploads to authenticated administrators with max size and image MIME constraints.
Actual Result: No storage rules in repository; client-side validation can be bypassed by any direct API call or modified client.
Technical Impact: Unchecked storage bucket access could allow arbitrary file uploads (HTML/SVG with embedded JS, malware) or unbounded storage consumption.
Business Impact: Cloud storage quota exhaustion, hosting malicious payloads under company domain, and unexpected cloud bills.
Remediation Recommendation: Create and deploy storage.rules requiring request.auth.token.admin == true, resource size < 5MB, and image/ contentType.

Defect Title: Unauthenticated Google Apps Script Webhook with Silent no-cors Error Masking
Description: In emailService.js (lines 1-33), order dispatch relies on a hardcoded Google Apps Script Webhook using fetch() with mode: "no-cors". Under no-cors, the response is opaque and the Promise resolves successfully regardless of whether Google Apps Script returned HTTP 200, 403, 500, or timed out.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Inspect emailService.js line 19.
2. Note mode: "no-cors" and return { success: true }.
3. Disconnect script endpoint or exhaust Google quota.
Expected Result: Order notification delivery should be verifiable, authenticated, and provide delivery status feedback.
Actual Result: emailService assumes success whenever the network request does not throw a socket error; failures in the Apps Script trigger silent notification drops.
Technical Impact: Silent failure of the primary notification channel alerting bakery staff to new orders.
Business Impact: Bakery staff miss customer orders, leading to delayed baking and missed delivery deadlines.
Remediation Recommendation: Replace Google Apps Script with Firebase Cloud Functions triggering SendGrid, Postmark, or Resend with authenticated API keys and delivery status receipts.

Defect Title: Massive Uncompressed Image Payload (>193MB Total, 2MB-3.5MB Per Asset) Degrading Mobile Performance
Description: The public/images directory contains 193.7 MB of uncompressed PNG files. Loading catalog pages like /gallery or /seasonal pulls dozens of 2.0MB to 3.5MB PNGs simultaneously, causing mobile network saturation and severe LCP delays.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Clear browser cache.
2. Open Chrome DevTools Network tab with Fast 3G or 4G throttling.
3. Load /seasonal or /gallery.
4. Observe transferred payload (>15MB) and load time (>8s).
Expected Result: Images should be compressed and formatted as WebP/AVIF (under 150KB each), using responsive sizes and lazy loading.
Actual Result: Uncompressed PNG images up to 3.5MB each loaded concurrently, blocking main thread and inflating page weight to 20MB+.
Technical Impact: Severe mobile performance degradation, excessive memory consumption, and Core Web Vitals LCP failure (>6.0s).
Business Impact: High bounce rate from mobile visitors in Ethiopia experiencing slow loading or high mobile data charges.
Remediation Recommendation: Convert all PNG assets to WebP with 80% quality compression (reducing total footprint from 193MB to <12MB), add loading="lazy", and implement srcset.

Defect Title: Fatal Runtime TypeError in Cart Total Calculation When Item Price Is Undefined or Null
Description: In CartContext.js (lines 60-64), getCartTotal() executes: item.price.toString().replace(/[^0-9.]/g, ""). If any item in the cart lacks a defined price property, calling .toString() throws a fatal unhandled TypeError, crashing the application or locking the cart.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Add an item to cart where price is undefined or null.
2. Open /cart or inspect cart total.
Expected Result: getCartTotal should safely handle null or undefined prices: (item.price ?? "").toString().
Actual Result: Application crashes with Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading "toString").
Technical Impact: Unhandled JavaScript runtime error crashing React rendering tree and freezing checkout navigation.
Business Impact: Customer cannot complete checkout, abandoned shopping carts, lost sales.
Remediation Recommendation: Defensively handle price: const priceRaw = item?.price != null ? String(item.price) : "";

Defect Title: 84 Known Security Vulnerabilities (4 Critical, 38 High) in Legacy Create-React-App Toolchain
Description: Running npm audit reveals 84 vulnerabilities across the project dependency tree (websocket-driver critical, webpack-dev-middleware high, react-router open redirect/XSS high, undici high, @grpc/grpc-js high). These are pinned by deprecated react-scripts 5.0.1.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Execute npm audit in project root.
2. Review reported CVEs and dependency paths.
Expected Result: Dependencies should be actively maintained with zero Critical or High known CVEs.
Actual Result: 84 vulnerabilities reported; react-scripts deprecation blocks standard npm audit fix without breaking changes.
Technical Impact: Vulnerable development server and bundled dependency vulnerabilities affecting build integrity and security posture.
Business Impact: Compliance failure, vulnerability to known exploits, and growing technical debt.
Remediation Recommendation: Migrate build system from deprecated react-scripts to Vite 5+ and update react-router-dom to latest secure release.

Defect Title: Default Create-React-App Metadata in Production HTML (<title>React App</title> & Boilerplate Description)
Description: The production HTML returned by https://goodnews-cake-and-catering.vercel.app/ retains default Create-React-App metadata: <title>React App</title> and <meta name="description" content="Web site created using create-react-app"/>.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Open https://goodnews-cake-and-catering.vercel.app/ in browser.
2. View page source or browser tab title.
Expected Result: Title should be "GoodNews Cake & Catering | Custom Cakes & Bakery in Addis Ababa" with tailored SEO description and OpenGraph tags.
Actual Result: Production browser tab displays "React App"; search engine snippet displays "Web site created using create-react-app".
Technical Impact: Zero keyword indexing for bakery services, broken social media link preview cards on Telegram/Facebook, and unprofessional appearance.
Business Impact: Loss of organic search traffic across Addis Ababa and poor social sharing engagement.
Remediation Recommendation: Update public/index.html with branded titles, rich meta description, OpenGraph/Twitter cards, and canonical URL.

Defect Title: Missing XML Sitemap File & Robots.txt Sitemap Reference; SPA Rewrite Traps Crawler
Description: There is no sitemap.xml in the public directory or repository. Requesting https://goodnews-cake-and-catering.vercel.app/sitemap.xml returns index.html (HTTP 200 text/html) due to Vercel SPA rewrite rules. robots.txt lacks a Sitemap: directive.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Execute: curl.exe -I https://goodnews-cake-and-catering.vercel.app/sitemap.xml
2. Inspect Content-Type and response body.
Expected Result: Requesting sitemap.xml should return valid application/xml listing all public routes (/gallery, /cupcakes, /cookies, /seasonal, /catering, /about).
Actual Result: Returns index.html; search engines parsing sitemap.xml receive HTML parser syntax errors.
Technical Impact: Search engine crawlers fail to discover deep product pages, catalog sections, and seasonal offerings.
Business Impact: Sub-optimal indexation in Google Search, resulting in lower search ranking for cake queries in Addis Ababa.
Remediation Recommendation: Create public/sitemap.xml listing all canonical URLs and add Sitemap: https://goodnews-cake-and-catering.vercel.app/sitemap.xml to public/robots.txt.

Defect Title: WCAG 2.2 Level AA Non-Compliance: Missing Form Labels, Unlabeled Icon Buttons, and Modal Focus Traps
Description: Form inputs across order modals lack explicit <label htmlFor="..."> connections; modal close buttons and search triggers lack aria-label attributes; interactive modals do not implement keyboard focus traps or ESC key listeners.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Run Lighthouse Accessibility audit or inspect modal markup in Gallery.jsx and Header.jsx.
2. Tab through open modal using keyboard only.
Expected Result: All inputs have associated programmatic labels; all icon buttons have aria-label; modals trap keyboard focus and dismiss on Escape.
Actual Result: Input controls rely solely on placeholders; icon-only buttons have no accessible names; focus escapes background while modal is open.
Technical Impact: Screen reader users and keyboard-only navigators cannot independently navigate forms or dismiss dialogs.
Business Impact: Accessibility barrier for disabled individuals, failure to meet WCAG 2.2 AA standards.
Remediation Recommendation: Add htmlFor/id pairings to all form fields, add aria-label to all icon buttons, and implement proper focus trapping in modals.

Defect Title: Malformed String Template in Home.jsx Initial State for heroBadge
Description: In Home.jsx (line 11), heroBadge is initialized with a literal string: "{heroContent.heroBadge || \"Where Every Bite Brings Joy\"}". While currently overridden by hardcoded JSX in line 102, this represents dead and malformed code.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Inspect Home.jsx line 11.
2. Note literal string assigned to heroBadge.
Expected Result: Initial state should be a clean fallback string: "Where Every Bite Brings Joy".
Actual Result: String contains unparsed JSX curly braces and logical OR syntax as literal characters.
Technical Impact: Code smell; will display broken syntax if dynamic rendering is restored.
Business Impact: Cosmetic confusion and poor code quality baseline.
Remediation Recommendation: Refactor Home.jsx line 11 to clean string: heroBadge: "Where Every Bite Brings Joy", and bind dynamically in JSX.

Defect Title: Footer Dead Anchor Link, Email Address Typo, and Unlinked Telephone Number
Description: In Footer.jsx: Line 23 has an Instagram link with href="#"; Line 59 has a typo in bakery email ("goodnewsscake@gmail.com" with two s's); Line 54 displays telephone number without a tel: URI link.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Inspect Footer.jsx lines 23, 54, 59.
2. Click Instagram icon and check URL.
Expected Result: Instagram should link to official profile or be conditionally omitted; email should match goodnewscake@gmail.com; phone should have tel: link.
Actual Result: Clicking Instagram scrolls page to top; email has typo; clicking phone does nothing.
Technical Impact: Dead links and misdirected customer emails.
Business Impact: Prospective customers attempting to email or view Instagram cannot reach the business.
Remediation Recommendation: Update Footer.jsx with active Instagram URL, correct email spelling, and wrap phone number in <a href="tel:+251917559943">.

Defect Title: Zero Application Test Coverage & Broken Default Create-React-App Test in Source Tree
Description: App.test.js contains only the default boilerplate test expecting /learn react/i, which immediately fails because the application does not render that text. There are zero functional, unit, or integration tests in the repository.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Run npm test -- --watchAll=false in project root.
2. Observe test failure.
Expected Result: Test suite should execute and pass unit tests covering core business logic (CartContext, statusUtils, orderService).
Actual Result: Test fails immediately with "Unable to find an element with the text: /learn react/i".
Technical Impact: Lack of automated regression detection; changes in one module can silently break other workflows without CI alerts.
Business Impact: High regression risk during future feature updates or bug fixes.
Remediation Recommendation: Replace boilerplate test with unit tests for CartContext (adding items, removing items, total calculation) and statusUtils.
